set.tagline: Buy the city, charge the rent, and hope your friends forget whose turn it is.
set.description: Property Rush is Boardit's free browser property-trading game for two to six players. Make a table, share its short code, buy cities, auction what others pass on and bargain your way out of rent you cannot pay.

systemRequirements.min: A current browser with JavaScript and an internet connection for online tables. Boardit does not publish CPU, RAM, GPU or installed-storage minimums.
systemRequirements.recommended: No numerical recommended hardware tier is published. Use a phone, tablet or desktop browser with a stable connection for a full table.

min.notes: Browser-based board game with no local installer. The developer provides no numerical CPU, RAM, GPU or storage requirement.

recommended.notes: No recommended hardware tier is published; a stable internet connection matters for online tables.

qualityBar.verdict: A property game where every unpaid bill turns into a negotiation with somebody who knows you are desperate.

set.longDescription:
Property Rush takes the familiar pleasure of buying a place your friends are about to land on and moves the whole argument into a browser. Two to six people can share a table. Buy a city nobody owns, collect rent when someone else arrives, and build houses to make that stop even more expensive. Own every city in a country and the rent doubles before the first house goes up, unless the host turns that rule off. A property that goes unbought enters an auction, which can be the moment a cautious player gives away the best deal of the night.

Boardit gives players ways to recover when the board turns against them. Trade with rivals, sell a holding or mortgage it to raise cash. If you cannot cover the full rent, the unpaid amount remains a debt rather than instantly throwing you out. You cannot roll while you owe money, so a seemingly minor shortfall can turn into a round of uncomfortable negotiations. The last player with money wins, or the table can end when everyone leaves. There is no automatic short round limit to save a group from its own stubbornness.

The turn timer gives those negotiations a shape. A player gets one minute for each turn and a small reserve of extra time for the whole game. When that runs out, a clearly labelled bot can finish a turn safely; after two missed turns it keeps the seat moving until the player returns. That is useful in a browser game where a dropped connection or a doorbell should not strand five other people. The host can also switch on faster dice and a Speed Die for a more restless table.

Getting people together is simple on the game's own terms. Create a room, send its five-character code and have friends join from phones, tablets or laptops. Guests do not need Boardit accounts. Open public tables and quick match are available, while bots can fill a table if nobody else is around. This is game-hosted online play, not a downloadable dedicated-server package or a virtual-LAN title. PlayBound has not verified automatic room-code handoff from its party screen, so use the game's Join with a code flow for now.

Property Rush runs in a browser without a local install, and Boardit publishes no numerical hardware sheet or physical-controller layout. Touch play on a phone is not the same claim as native gamepad support on a PC. The appeal here is social rather than technical: a city that looks like a bargain on your turn becomes a trap when someone else owns the next square. We are keeping the game in Draft until a full human table has tested its pace, but its rules and joining steps can already be stated plainly.
set.whyWePickedIt: A short room code, guest access and tables for two to six make Property Rush easy to bring to a group. Its debt and auction rules give friends reasons to bargain instead of just rolling and waiting. We still want a full-table play test before a final quality verdict.
set.thatOneThing: Miss two turns and a bot takes your seat. Your friends may decide they prefer negotiating with it.

installSteps.text: Open Boardit's Property Rush page in a current browser. The game is free to play and has no local installer.
Create a room and share its five-character code. Friends can choose Join with a code on their own phones, tablets or computers; guest play needs no Boardit account.
Choose the table rules in the lobby and start when seats are filled. You can add clearly labelled bots if fewer than six people are present.

firstPlaySteps.text: Watch auctions on unbought cities and the rent bonus for owning a complete country before spending everything on one square.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: Use Property Rush's own five-character room code to join friends. PlayBound has not yet verified automatic code transfer from its party screen.
